title: Hip Thrust Machine
summary: A hip thrust with a padded belt or lever instead of a barbell, so it's quick to set up and comfortable on the hips.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: commercial gym machine (this exercise's own machine).

muscles.why: Library rating 1 for glutes (main mover): each working set adds 1 of a set to the weekly glutes total.
Library rating 0.3 for hamstrings (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly hamstrings total.
Library rating 0.3 for adductors (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly adductors total.
Library rating 0.25 for quads (minor): each working set adds 0.25 of a set to the weekly quads total.

setup.text: Sit with your upper back on the pad and the belt or pad across your hips.
Drive through your heels to lift your hips until they're in line with your body.
Squeeze at the top, then lower under control.

form_cues.cue: Squeeze the glutes at the top
Keep your chin tucked and your ribs down. Finish with your glutes, not your back.

mistakes.text: Overextending the lower back at the top.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds up to 2 ramp-up sets only when the load is heavy for the equipment and the main muscle is not warm yet.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 7.5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 8-12 reps, stopping about 3 reps short of failure (RIR 3). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train pain-free.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: One side at a time, Less systemic fatigue, Lower loading potential.
